memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "A people has come out of Egypt; they cover the face of the land and have settled next to me. Now come and put a curse on these people, because they are too powerful for me. Perhaps then I will be able to defeat them and drive them out of the country. For I know that whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed." - Num 22:5b-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balak's message to Balaam lays his heart bare. He wants a curse placed on Israel so he can defeat them. He even flatters Balaam, crediting him with the power to make blessing and cursing stick. In Balak's mind, the right words from the right man could turn the tide.

But Balak has misunderstood something fundamental. Blessing and cursing are not powers that men wield at will; they rest in the hands of God alone. No hired prophet could overturn what the Lord had determined for His people. Balak was setting himself against the purposes of the Almighty without even realising it.

There is deep comfort here for the people of God. Israel was utterly unaware of this plot unfolding in the courts of Moab. While they camped by the Jordan, a king was scheming to have them cursed. Yet they were perfectly safe, because their God was watching over them.

The same is true for those who belong to Christ. There is no curse, no scheme, no hidden plot that can undo God's love for His people. If God is for us, who can be against us? No weapon formed against you will finally prevail (Rom 8:31; Isa 54:17), for you are held secure in Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you rest in the truth that God watches over you, even in unseen dangers?
2. Where do you need to trust that no scheme can overturn God's purposes?
3. How does God's protection of Israel encourage your own security in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that no curse or scheme can undo Your love for me. When unseen dangers surround me, help me rest secure in Your watchful care through Christ. Amen.
